Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid is indicated for the treatment of uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTIs) caused by Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Proteus mirabilis in women who have limited or no alternative oral antibacterial treatment options. The recommended dosage is one tablet (sulopenem etzadroxil 500 mg/probenecid 500 mg) taken orally twice daily for 5 days with food. The safety and efficacy of this combination have not been fully established. 2. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid increases the plasma levels of ketorolac by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for increased adverse effects. 3. Probenecid, an inhibitor of organic anion transporters (OAT1/3), may increase the plasma concentrations of drugs that rely on OAT1/3 for elimination. This can lead to elevated drug levels and an increased risk of adverse reactions. 4. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid increases the plasma levels of ketoprofen by decreasing its metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug due to the potential for increased toxicity. 5. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid increases the plasma levels of methotrexate by decreasing its metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative therapy. If coadministration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring for methotrexate-associated adverse reactions is necessary, as outlined in its prescribing information. 6. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid decreases the efficacy of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may reduce the effectiveness of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. It is recommended to complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 7. Caution is advised, and frequent monitoring for adverse reactions such as diarrhea and nausea is recommended. 8. Probenecid’s inhibition of OAT1/3 may increase the risk of hypoglycemia. Refer to glimepiride-specific prescribing information for dosage adjustments. 10.
